problem:
A particle $P$ is traveling along the $x$-axis with displacement $s(t)$ from a fixed origin $O$ given by

$$
s(t)=-\frac{2}{9}{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2}+14t+17,\,t\ge 0.
$$

Find the time at which the acceleration is zero, and find the value of the velocity at this moment.
worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{2}{9}{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2}+14t+17) \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}{t}^{2}+6t+14\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{2}{3}{t}^{2}+6t+14) \\  & =-\frac{4}{3}t+6\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we put $a=0$ to find the time when the acceleration is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =-\frac{4}{3}t+6 \\ \frac{4}{3}t & =6 \\ t & =4.5\end{aligned}
$$

So the acceleration is zero when $t=4.5.$ To find the velocity at this moment, we substitute this back into $v(t)$ to get

$$
v(4.5)=-\frac{2}{3}(4.5)^{2}+6(4.5)+14=27.5.
$$
